categories.name: Vegetable Gardening
categories.intro: Growing your own vegetables is one of the most satisfying things a garden can offer. These ideas cover sunny beds, shady corners, small balconies and big backyards, with practical advice on soil health, compost, sunlight, plant spacing, watering and sowing times. You will find layouts for tomatoes, leafy greens, root vegetables and beans, plus crop rotation and succession sowing, and natural ways to keep pests down without chemicals. Whether you plant your first lettuce or plan a full kitchen garden, start here and grow food you will love to eat.

categories.name: Container Gardening
categories.intro: No yard? No problem. Container gardening lets you grow herbs, vegetables and flowers on a balcony, patio, doorstep or sunny windowsill. These ideas show which pots, potting mix, compost and drainage work best — never garden soil in pots — how often to water, and how to group plants that like the same sunlight and soil. From self-watering planters to stacked strawberry towers, you will find practical, low-cost ways to start growing today, even if all you have is one sunny corner.

categories.name: Raised Beds
categories.intro: Raised beds give you better soil, better drainage and a garden that is easier on your back. These ideas cover cedar, stone and recycled-material beds in every size, plus layouts for vegetables, herbs and flowers. You will learn how deep to build, what compost-rich soil mix to fill beds with, and how to arrange plants — spacing, sunlight, watering and companion planting — so every inch earns its keep. Whether you have a tiny courtyard or a full backyard, a raised bed is the fastest way to a productive garden.

categories.name: Herb Gardens
categories.intro: Fresh herbs turn ordinary cooking into something special, and they are among the easiest plants to grow. These ideas cover windowsill pots in full sunlight, kitchen-door herb spirals, shady mint patches and full herb beds, with tips on soil, watering, pruning and harvesting so your plants stay productive all season. Grow basil, rosemary, mint, parsley and more — learn which herbs are perennial, which need re-sowing each spring, and how to dry or freeze the harvest for winter cooking.

categories.name: Flower Beds
categories.intro: Flower beds are where a garden shows its personality. These ideas mix colour, height and bloom season so your beds look good from spring to autumn, with planting plans for borders in full sunlight, shady corners and pollinator-friendly spaces. You will find combinations that work in real soil, compost and real weather — perennials for structure, annuals for instant colour — plus deadheading, watering and simple care routines that keep blooms coming. Start with one bed, and let the colour spread from there.

categories.name: Indoor Plants
categories.intro: Indoor plants bring life to every room, clean the air and ask for very little in return. These ideas cover low-light survivors, statement floor plants, trailing vines for shelves and easy-care collections for beginners. You will learn which plants suit each room, how much light, water and humidity they need, when to repot and propagate, and how to spot trouble early — yellow leaves, root rot and pests. Whether you want one hardy plant or a full indoor jungle, there is a green companion here for your home.

categories.name: Seasonal Planting Guides
categories.intro: Good gardens follow the seasons. These guides tell you what to plant, sow and harvest in spring, summer, autumn and winter, so you always know what to do next. You will find month-by-month checklists, last frost dates explained simply, hardiness zones and sowing calendars, and succession sowing ideas for keeping colour and food coming all year. Follow the season, work with your climate, and your garden will reward you in every month of the year.
